prompt: Which two packages does the course's recommended path install on Ubuntu 24.04?
hint: One line of `apt` installs both.

choices.text: `openjdk-25-jre-headless` and `maven`
choices.why: The `-jre` package is a runtime: it runs programs and cannot compile one, which is section 04's second failure.

choices.text: `openjdk-25-jdk` and `maven`
choices.why: Right: the JDK for compiling and running, and Maven for building projects from lesson 18 on.

choices.text: `default-jdk` and `maven`, so that Ubuntu picks the version
choices.why: Ubuntu 24.04's default is 21, chosen before 25 existed; the course asks for 25 by name.

choices.text: `openjdk-21-jdk` and `maven`, because Maven depends on 21
choices.why: Maven pulls in a Java 21 runtime by itself; the course still installs and uses the 25 JDK.

prompt: Before it downloaded anything, `apt` said how much disk the installation would take. How many megabytes?
hint: The line starts with `After this operation`.

prompt: Your computer runs Windows and you want every transcript in the course to match your screen exactly. Which path does the section point you to?
hint: The transcripts were recorded on one particular system.

choices.text: A cloud development environment in the browser
choices.why: It costs your computer nothing, but its JDK is another build in other directories, so paths differ.

choices.text: A JDK 25 installer for Windows itself
choices.why: That runs Java, but the prompts, paths and `apt` commands of the course would not exist on your screen.

choices.text: Ubuntu 24.04 in WSL or another virtual machine
choices.why: Right: with Ubuntu inside, the installed path runs as printed, prompt and all.

prompt: Ana installed one JDK, yet `/usr/lib/jvm` holds a Java 21 as well. Where did it come from?
hint: Look at what `apt-cache depends` printed.

choices.text: Ubuntu 24.04 ships it preinstalled on every system
choices.why: The bare machine answered `java: command not found` before the install, so there was no Java at all.

choices.text: Maven depends on the archive's default runtime, which is 21
choices.why: Right: `maven` needs `default-jre-headless`, and in 24.04 that is `openjdk-21-jre-headless`.

choices.text: `openjdk-25-jdk` includes the previous LTS for compatibility
choices.why: The 25 package carries only 25; compatibility comes from `--release`, in section 06.

choices.text: `update-alternatives` downloads a fallback in case 25 breaks
choices.why: `update-alternatives` only manages links between JDKs already installed; it installs nothing.

prompt: With both 21 and 25 installed, why does typing `java` run 25?
hint: `update-alternatives --display java` said which mode it is in.

choices.text: The shell always runs the most recently installed program
choices.why: The shell runs whatever `/usr/bin/java` points at; installation order does not decide it.

choices.text: In auto mode the alternative with the highest priority wins, and 25 has 2511
choices.why: Right: 2511 beats 21's 2111, so the link points at the 25 directory.

choices.text: `JAVA_HOME` points at 25 after the installation
choices.why: `JAVA_HOME` was never set on this machine; section 04 shows what happens when it is.

choices.text: A runtime without a compiler cannot be run directly
choices.why: The 21 runtime runs programs perfectly well; section 04 runs one with it.

prompt: Match each JDK program to what it does.
hint: The table in the section.

pairs.right: Starts a JVM and runs a program in it
Prints what is inside a `.class` file
Runs Java one line at a time

right_distractors: Downloads a newer JDK when a project asks for one

prompt: `sudo apt install -y openjdk-25-jdk` answers `E: Unable to locate package openjdk-25-jdk`. What do you try first?
hint: `apt` installs from a list it keeps on disk.

choices.text: Download a JDK archive from a vendor's website instead
choices.why: That works around a list that is merely stale, and leaves you with a JDK outside the course's paths.

choices.text: `sudo apt update`, then the install again
choices.why: Right: the package list is only as recent as the last update, and a fresh machine may never have had one.

choices.text: Install `openjdk-21-jdk`, since 25 is not packaged for 24.04
choices.why: It is packaged: `apt-cache policy` named 25.0.4.1 as the candidate once the list was updated.

choices.text: Reinstall Ubuntu, since the archive configuration is broken
choices.why: Nothing was broken; one `apt update` fixed it.

prompt: A setup script runs `sudo apt install -y openjdk-25-jdk | tail -3` and then checks `$?`, which is 0. The package was not installed. Why did the check pass?
hint: Which command's status does `$?` hold after a pipe?

choices.text: `apt` returns 0 whenever it finishes reading its package list
choices.why: `apt` did fail; the number on the screen just was not its number.

choices.text: `-y` turns every error into a warning
choices.why: `-y` only answers yes to the confirmation question; it changes no exit status.

choices.text: `$?` is the status of `tail`, the last command of the pipe
choices.why: Right: `tail` succeeded, so the pipe did, and `apt`'s failure was hidden.

prompt: `java -version` prints 25, and `javac -version` prints `javac: command not found` with exit status 127. What is installed?
hint: 127 is the shell talking, not Java.

choices.text: A Java 25 runtime package, without the development kit
choices.why: Right: a `-jre` package runs programs and has no compiler; `openjdk-25-jdk` adds it.

choices.text: A full JDK whose `javac` was removed from `PATH` by `update-alternatives`
choices.why: `update-alternatives` registers `javac` too; with a JDK installed, `javac` answers.

choices.text: A JDK 25 and a JDK 21 that disagree about which compiler to use
choices.why: Two JDKs would give you two compilers, not none.

choices.text: Maven alone, which brings a `java` and no compiler
choices.why: Maven brings Java 21's runtime; the `java -version` here said 25.

prompt: A guide tells you to add `export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/default-java` to `~/.profile`. On the course's machine, what does that change?
hint: Where does `default-java` point?

choices.text: Nothing, because `default-java` is the link to the newest JDK
choices.why: `default-java` points at 21, the archive's default when 24.04 was released.

choices.text: Every `java` command in the shell starts running 21
choices.why: The shell's `java` still follows `/usr/bin/java`; `JAVA_HOME` is read by tools such as Maven.

choices.text: Maven starts running on Java 21, with nothing on screen saying so
choices.why: Right: `mvn -v` showed 21 with that value set, and a project asking for 25 then fails.

prompt: What does `javac Hello.java` produce?
hint: Look at what `ls -l` listed afterwards.

choices.text: An executable for this processor, called `Hello`
choices.why: That is what a C compiler does; `javac` writes bytecode, not machine code.

choices.text: `Hello.class`, bytecode for the Java Virtual Machine
choices.why: Right: 415 bytes of bytecode, and `java Hello` runs it.

choices.text: Nothing on disk: it compiles and runs the program in one step
choices.why: `java Hello.java` can do that, as lesson 2 shows; `javac` writes a file and runs nothing.

choices.text: A `.jar` archive holding the class and its source
choices.why: A `.jar` is made by the `jar` tool, or by Maven in lesson 18.

prompt: Every class file starts with the same four bytes, written in hexadecimal as `___`.
hint: `od` printed them, and `file` recognised the file by them.

prompt: `javap -c Hello` printed two methods, and `Hello.java` declares only `main`. What is the other one?
hint: Its name is the class's name.

choices.text: A copy of `main` the JIT compiler prepared in advance
choices.why: The JIT works while the program runs, in memory; it never writes into the class file.

choices.text: The `println` method, copied in from `System.out`
choices.why: `println` is called with `invokevirtual`; its code stays in the JDK's library.

choices.text: A constructor the compiler wrote because the class declares none
choices.why: Right: `public Hello()` calls `Object`'s constructor and returns; lesson 13 explains why it is there.

prompt: Put the four bytecode instructions of `main` in the order the JVM runs them.
hint: First the object, then the argument, then the call.

prompt: A program spends a minute in one loop. What does the JVM do with that loop's method while the program runs?
hint: The JVM counts while it interprets.

choices.text: It keeps interpreting it one instruction at a time, as it does all bytecode
choices.why: Interpreting is only the start; a method called often enough is compiled.

choices.text: It compiles it into the processor's own instructions, and runs those instead
choices.why: Right: that is the JIT compiler, and it is why such a program speeds up in its first seconds.

choices.text: It asks `javac` to recompile the source with optimisations
choices.why: The JVM never calls `javac` and often has no source to give it.

choices.text: It writes a faster version of the method into `Hello.class` for the next run
choices.why: Compiled code lives in the process's memory and goes when the process ends; the class file is unchanged.

prompt: How often does a new Java feature release come out?
hint: Every March and every September, since Java 10.

choices.text: Once a year
choices.why: Twice a year; the yearly count would miss half the releases.

choices.text: Every six months
choices.why: Right: and every two years one of them is an LTS release.

choices.text: Every two years
choices.why: That is the LTS rhythm; the feature releases come four times as often.

choices.text: When a large feature is ready
choices.why: That was the rule until 2017, and gaps ran to five years; now the date is fixed and the features wait.

prompt: A class file's major version is 61. Which Java release compiled it? Give the release number.
hint: The major version is the release plus 44.

prompt: Your team compiles on JDK 25, and the server that runs the program has Java 21. What do you add to the compilation, and why that rather than anything else?
hint: It is one flag of `javac`.

choices.text: Nothing: a JVM runs every class file version, older or newer
choices.why: Only older or equal: 21 refuses version 69 with `UnsupportedClassVersionError`.

choices.text: `--release 21`, which also refuses any library call 21 does not have
choices.why: Right: the class files get version 65, and a method that only exists in 25 fails at compile time, not on the server.

choices.text: Edit the class file's major version from 69 to 65
choices.why: The JVM would load it, and then fail the first time the code used something 21 lacks.

choices.text: Install JDK 25 on the server instead
choices.why: That works when you own the server, and the question is how to build for the one you have.

prompt: `java -version` prints `openjdk version "25.0.4.1"`. What does the `4` say?
hint: Four positions: feature, interim, update, patch.

choices.text: That this is the fourth JDK installed on the machine
choices.why: The version string describes the build, not the machine.

choices.text: That the build is for the fourth Ubuntu release of the year
choices.why: Ubuntu's part of the string comes after `build`, in the second line.

choices.text: That it is the fourth update of release 25
choices.why: Right: security and bug-fix updates move this number inside the same release.

choices.text: That the class files it writes have minor version 4
choices.why: Class files carry the major version 69 for 25; the update number is not written into them.

prompt: Which of these would make `java Hello` fail with `UnsupportedClassVersionError`? Choose all that apply.
hint: A JVM runs every version up to its own.

choices.text: Compiling with JDK 25 and running with the Java 21 that came with Maven
choices.why: Yes: version 69 on a JVM that recognises up to 65, which is the transcript in section 04.

choices.text: Compiling with `--release 8` and running with Java 25
choices.why: No: version 52 ran on 25 without a word in section 06.

choices.text: Compiling with JDK 25 and copying the class file to a server with Java 17
choices.why: Yes: 17 recognises up to 61, and the file says 69.

choices.text: Compiling with `--release 21` and running with the Java 21 runtime
choices.why: No: that writes version 65, which 21 recognises; it is the fix section 06 describes.
